gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-bree-serif: Impact Label hits hard, each letter standing alone with its own space. Bree Serif, a classic serif, gives paragraphs a literary, refined feel, its outsized lowercase carrying the eye steadily along.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-quando: Commanding and heavy, Impact Label stands its letters apart, each one set high and alone. Quando, with sparse letter spacing, reads in a bookish, traditional way across a whole page of text.
gen-dafont-impact-label-outfit: Heavy and commanding, Impact Label puts each letter on its own. Outfit is clean and approachable, its moderate lowercase and curves that stop short of closing letting long text flow easily.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-fs-amulya: Jelly Crazies wobbles playfully, its bowls nearly sealed shut and its pace slowing to a leisurely walk. Amulya keeps its curve gaps generous, so text feels modern and open.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-fs-chillax: Chillax lays its line out like spaghetti, with pen-lifted curves leaving each loop unfinished. Chillax then sits opposite Jelly Crazies, whose bowls nearly seal shut, so open and closed shapes trade places.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-gf-almendra: Jelly Crazies is playful and wobbly, drawn with no calligraphic thinning at all. Wobble is what it does best, while Almendra, a serif, does dignified, bookish text with its deep lowercase midsection.
gen-dafont-jelly-crazies-plus-jakarta-sa: Plus Jakarta Sans is modern and precise, built from one monoline stroke. The standout quality is closed against open: Jelly Crazies nearly seals its bowls, while the sans keeps its curves apart.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-bitter: Loosely tracked, single-width rolling-ball strokes give Lemon Milk a neon-tube look, wide and friendly, rounded letters staying open and inviting. Bitter, a slab-serif, adds a grounded, dependable counterweight below.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-fs-roundo: Friendly and striking, Lemon Milk runs wide and loosely tracked, its rounded letters staying open and inviting. Roundo does the quieter work, its moderate lowercase and uncluttered counters suiting text.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noto-rashi-hebr: Noto Rashi Hebrew is classic, with faint contrast like lightly engraved brass. Lemon Milk is best at being striking, wide and single-width; the Rashi face is best at quiet, bookish text with short ascenders.
